text:
Seattle didn't just win at Capital One Arena, it won the way the shot quality said it should. The Kraken created 5.03 expected goals to Washington's 3.35, and in simulated replays of every shot they came out ahead 60 percent of the time. Even with penalties set aside, at 3.51 to 2.84, they held the better of the chances. The edge showed up in every period and was widest in the third, 2.48 to 1.65.

The first period was a seesaw. Kaapo Kakko's snap shot opened the scoring at 6:06, then Jordan Kyrou and Alex Ovechkin put Washington up 2-1 on a pair of low-probability chances (13 and 16 percent). Jordan Eberle answered with 11 seconds left in the period, an 8 percent look that tied it. Frederick Gaudreau's backhand put Seattle ahead in the second, and Boone Jenner tied it again 46 seconds into the third, one of five shots he put on goal.

The decider came late. Jared McCann's snap shot at 14:33 broke the tie, and Ryan Winterton added an empty-looking 85 percent chance at 17:20 to close it out at 5-3. Washington outattempted Seattle 60 to 56, but Logan Thompson allowed 5 goals against 3.91 expected, a shade over a goal worse than the chances warranted. Joey Daccord faced 36 shots and stopped nearly all of what the model expected, finishing slightly ahead of it.
